notes.1: Almost all candidates resolved forces vertically and horizontally, but many candidates obtained inaccurate answers because of approximation of sinα and cosα, and because they used the incorrect trigonometric ratios. Answer: F = 1.6
notes.2: Both parts of this question were attempted well, although some candidates gave the answer for part (ii) as ‘the weight is 8 kg.’ Answer: (i) 1000 J (ii) 80 N
notes.3: This question was well attempted, especially part (ii). Answer: (i) F = 103 (ii) 122.5 m
notes.4i: This part of the question was well attempted, although many candidates did not state the decelerations but gave the answers as a = –2 ms–2 and a = – 2.5 ms–2 for P and Q respectively.
notes.4iii: Many candidates could not decide a strategy for finding the speeds of P and Q at the required instant. Answer: (i) 2 ms–2, 2.5ms–2 (ii) 6.09 ms–1, 0.614 ms–1
notes.5i: Candidates who found the driving force and multiplied it by the length of the hill usually found the correct answer for the work done by the driving force. Most candidates who used work/energy calculated the gain in potential energy and the work done against the resistance, then usually added these quantities together to obtain the correct answer.
notes.5iii: Most candidates obtained a simple equation in d (the required distance) by equating the work done by the engine with the sum of the increase in kinetic energy and the work done against the resistance. Almost all of these candidates found the correct answer for the required distance. Answer: (i) 4.99 × 106 J (ii) 1500 m
notes.6i: This part was attempted completely and correctly by almost all candidates.
notes.6iii: Most candidates obtained the distance travelled by each of the particles while the string is taut. However many candidates did not use s = ut + ½ gt2 with s the distance that A falls from the time the string breaks until A reaches the floor, and u = –1.6. Answer: (i) 4.2 N (ii) 0.6 s
notes.7i: This part was reasonably well attempted by those who recognised the need to use calculus.
notes.7iii: Very few candidates recognised the need to use v(10) = 30 to obtain the constant term of 50 in the expression for v(t) and similarly very few used s(10) = 100 to obtain the constant term of –1000/3 in the expression for s(t). Answer: (i) Velocity = 30 ms–1, displacement = 100 m (ii) 194 m
notes.key_messages:
• It is important for candidates to read the question carefully, and answer as required.
• Attention needs to be paid to making sure workings are carried out at a sufficient level of accuracy to
ensure the accuracy of the final answer.
